Title: Add ChatGPT proxy credential support and managed Codex responses websocket support · Pull Request #24983 · BerriAI/litellm
URL: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/24983
Published: 2026-04-02T00:00:00.000Z
Author: mookim-eth
Highlights:
## Relevant issues 
 
 LiteLLM's current ChatGPT proxy + Codex flow has several gaps that this PR addresses: 
 
- ChatGPT credentials can only be configured in static config today; they cannot be added cleanly from the proxy UI, and there is no deployment-scoped auth file path support. In practice this limits proxy usage to a single ChatGPT account. 
- ChatGPT auth may fall back to interactive device-code login, which is not safe for proxy/server environments and can block LiteLLM Proxy web service startup or request handling when auth is missing. 
- `session_id` is not consistently propagated through the proxy path, which can break request chaining and prompt cache behavior for Codex sessions. 
- Fallbacks to ChatGPT can include unsupported fields such as `metadata`, causing the initial request and the retry/fallback path to fail for the same reason. 
- Codex opens a WebSocket connection to the Responses API and does not always provide `model` in the query string during handshake, which can cause the current proxy websocket path to reject the request (HTTP 403) before it reaches normal handling. 
 
 This PR makes ChatGPT proxy credentials deployment-scoped, fails fast when non-interactive ChatGPT auth is unavailable, preserves `session_id` propagation, removes unsupported fields from ChatGPT fallback requests, and supports the Codex-style Responses API websocket flow.

Use ChatGPT Pro/Max subscription models through LiteLLM with OAuth device flow authentication.

| Supported Endpoints | `/responses`, `/chat/completions` (bridged to Responses for supported models) |
| API Reference | https://chatgpt.com |
...
ChatGPT subscription access is native to the Responses API. Chat Completions requests are bridged to Responses for supported models (for example `chatgpt/gpt-5.4`).
...
- The ChatGPT subscription backend rejects token limit fields (`max_tokens`, `max_output_tokens`, `max_completion_tokens`) and `metadata`. LiteLLM strips these fields for this provider.
- `/v1/chat/completions` honors `stream`. When `stream` is false (default), LiteLLM aggregates the Responses stream into a single JSON response.
...
ChatGPT subscription access uses an OAuth device code flow:
...
1. LiteLLM prints a device code and verification URL
2. Open the URL, sign in, and enter the code
3. Tokens are stored locally for reuse
...

Title: Add ChatGPT proxy credential support and managed Codex responses websocket support · Pull Request #24983 · BerriAI/litellm
URL: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/24983
Published: 2026-04-02T00:00:00.000Z
Author: mookim-eth
Highlights:
## Relevant issues 
 
 LiteLLM's current ChatGPT proxy + Codex flow has several gaps that this PR addresses: 
 
- ChatGPT credentials can only be configured in static config today; they cannot be added cleanly from the proxy UI, and there is no deployment-scoped auth file path support. In practice this limits proxy usage to a single ChatGPT account. 
- ChatGPT auth may fall back to interactive device-code login, which is not safe for proxy/server environments and can block LiteLLM Proxy web service startup or request handling when auth is missing. 
- `session_id` is not consistently propagated through the proxy path, which can break request chaining and prompt cache behavior for Codex sessions. 
- Fallbacks to ChatGPT can include unsupported fields such as `metadata`, causing the initial request and the retry/fallback path to fail for the same reason. 
- Codex opens a WebSocket connection to the Responses API and does not always provide `model` in the query string during handshake, which can cause the current proxy websocket path to reject the request (HTTP 403) before it reaches normal handling. 
 
 This PR makes ChatGPT proxy credentials deployment-scoped, fails fast when non-interactive ChatGPT auth is unavailable, preserves `session_id` propagation, removes unsupported fields from ChatGPT fallback requests, and supports the Codex-style Responses API websocket flow.

## Changes 
 
 This PR adds ChatGPT proxy credential support and managed Responses API websocket support for Codex-style workflows. 
 
 ### ChatGPT proxy credential support 
 - add request-scoped `chatgpt_auth_file_path` support to LiteLLM params 
 - resolve ChatGPT auth per request using the configured auth file path and api base 
 - fail fast when ChatGPT auth is unavailable and interactive login is disabled 
 - update ChatGPT Responses transformations to support proxy usage by: 
 - allowing `prompt_cache_key` 
 - dropping unsupported `metadata` 
 - preserving ChatGPT-specific request shaping and headers 
 
 ### Managed Codex responses websocket support

 - support resolving the model from the first websocket message when it is not present in the query string 
 - normalize proxy/router-facing model aliases to deployment params before backend calls 
 - support in-memory multi-turn session history for websocket response chains 
 - normalize websocket error payloads for Codex clients 
 - preserve request/session chain propagation used by websocket-based flows

## [BETA] Route all .completions requests to Responses API (better quality)​
...
When enabled, LiteLLM sends OpenAI traffic from`litellm.completion()` and the proxy`/chat/completions` endpoint through the Responses API instead of Chat Completions. That path generally matches OpenAI’s latest model behavior and quality (for example, reasoning output on GPT‑5 class models).

LiteLLM offers a chat completion to Responses API bridge. This lets you use the completion interface while calling the Responses API under the hood.

content.text: I've gathered the cluster conventions and the current (2026) state of LiteLLM's ChatGPT-subscription support from both docs and GitHub. Before I finalize the plan, a few decisions materially change the shape of the design. Let me confirm these

questions.question: The biggest architectural fork is how OAuth credentials persist. ChatGPT subscription auth stores a token `auth.json` that LiteLLM refresh-updates in place (write). Options differ on replicas:

options.label: Single replica + PV token file (Recommended)
options.description: Replicas=1, auth.json on a local-path PV pinned to s145. Simplest, matches LiteLLM's documented config. Downside: no HA. Refresh writes to the PV are fine with one pod.

options.label: Multi-replica + Postgres credential store
options.description: Replicas>1 using the newer DB-backed ChatGPT store (LiteLLM_CredentialsTable, STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True). Tokens survive in Postgres; scales to N replicas. Newer/less battle-tested in the community.

questions.question: What hostname should LiteLLM be exposed on? Your existing apps use *.beijns.eu.org via Cloudflare.

options.label: litellm.beijns.eu.org
options.description: New subdomain, Cloudflare DNS-01 cert via Traefik (existing resolver). Private + TLS.

options.label: Reuse existing / different hostname
options.description: Tell me the exact hostname you want (e.g. ai3.beijns.eu.org).

questions.question: Which upstream ChatGPT models should I configure as aliases? ChatGPT Plus entitlement differs from Pro. Only configure ones your account can actually use.

options.label: Verify-then-configure (Recommended)
options.description: Seed configs conservatively (e.g. gpt-5.x-codex, gpt-5.4-mini, chat-latest) and, after the device-flow login, query the ChatGPT backend to confirm entitlement and prune any Pro-only models before going live.

options.label: I know my entitlement
options.description: You'll tell me exactly which Codex/gpt-5.x models your Plus account can access.

questions.question: How do you want the deployment delivered? Your cluster uses Flux GitOps for immich/garage.

options.label: Flux HelmRelease + SOPS (Recommended)
options.description: Flux-managed Helm release in anywhere/k8s/litellm/, cluster Kustomization in clusters/s145/, secrets as SOPS. Mirrors immich. reconcile via 'flux reconcile kustomization'.

options.label: Plain manifests (kubectl apply)
options.description: Hand a-raw Deployment/Service/IngressRoute applied manually like vaultwarden.

Title: [Bug]: Helm chart default image tag main-<appVersion> does not exist on ghcr for stable releases → ImagePullBackOff · Issue #29348 · BerriAI/litellm
URL: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/29348
Published: 2026-05-30T00:00:00.000Z
Author: aSauerwein
Highlights:
# [Bug]: Helm chart default image tag main- does not exist on ghcr for stable releases → ImagePullBackOff
...
Installing `oci://ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-helm` with no `image.tag` override fails with `ImagePullBackOff`. The chart's default renders an image tag that is **not published** to `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database`.
...
`templates/deployment.yaml` and `templates/migrations-job.yaml` both default the tag to `main- `:
...
```yaml
image: "{{ .Values.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.image.tag | default (printf "main-%s" .Chart.AppVersion) }}"
```
...
For chart 1.86.2 (`AppVersion: 1.86.2`) this renders `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database:main-1.86.2`, which returns **404**. The registry has the plain `1.86.2` tag (and `main-stable`), but not `main-1.86.2`.
...
Anonymous manifest checks on `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database`:

| Chart version | `main- ` (default) | ` ` (plain) |
|---|---|---|
| 1.84.0 / 1.84.1 / 1.84.3 | 404 | 200 |
| 1.85.0 / 1.85.1 / 1.85.2 | 404 | 200 |
| 1.86.1 / 1.86.2 | 404 | 200 |
...
The published `1.86.2` tag and `main-stable` resolve to the **same digest** (`sha256:7b4494a6b2e366bf17ece8e3a84a5a92d5ce6c9309115cc6d65d71766fc59242`), confirming the image exists — only the `main- ` tag the chart constructs is missing.
...
A default install of any recent stable chart version cannot pull the app/migrations image; pods sit in `ImagePullBackOff` until the user manually overrides `image.tag`. Affects both the main Deployment and the DB migrations Job.
...
```yaml
image:
  tag: "1.86.2"   # immutable; same digest as main-stable
```
...
Either publish a `main- ` tag as part of the stable release pipeline, or change the chart's default to `.Chart.AppVersion` (the plain ` ` tag is consistently published).
...

helm template litellm oci://ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-helm --version 1.86.2 | grep litellm-database

Title: Production Deployment
URL: https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/deploy
Published: N/A
Author: N/A
Highlights:
- Monolithic: one`litellm` image serves LLM traffic, management APIs, and the UI. This is what the`litellm-helm` chart runs, and the simplest to operate.
- Microservices: a`gateway`(LLM traffic, port 4000),`backend`(management APIs and UI backend, port 4001), and`ui`(port 3000), each deployed and scaled independently. This is what the componentized`litellm` chart and both Terraform modules run; see the chart values for the full reference.
...
Official images are published to`ghcr.io/berriai` and mirrored at`docker.litellm.ai/berriai`. Use`ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database` for monolithic deployments with Postgres (it bundles the Prisma toolchain), and pin a version tag rather than`latest` or a moving tag, so rollbacks are deterministic. All images are signed; see the Docker Image Security Guide for verification and the non-root variant.
...
```yaml
replicaCount: 3image:  repository: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database  tag: "v1.90.2"          # pin your versionmasterkeySecretName: litellm-masterkeymasterkeySecretKey: masterkeydb:  useExisting: true  deployStandalone: false  endpoint: "<postgres-endpoint>"  database: litellm  secret:    name: litellm-db    usernameKey: username    passwordKey: passwordenvironmentSecrets:  - litellm-envproxy_config:  model_list:    - model_name: gpt-4o      litellm_params:        model: openai/gpt-4o        api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY  router_settings:    redis_host: "<redis-endpoint>"    redis_port: 6379    redis_password: os.environ/REDIS_PASSWORD
```
...
```bash
helm install litellm oci://ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-helm -f values.yaml
```
...
The chart lives at helm/litellm-helm; the published chart versions carry LiteLLM release numbers (for example`1.90.2`), and`helm show values oci://ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-helm` lists every knob. Beyond the values above it supports autoscaling (`autoscaling.*` or`keda.*`), PodDisruptionBudgets (`pdb.*`), a Prometheus ServiceMonitor (`serviceMonitor.*`), read replica routing (`db.readReplicaUrl`, see Database Read Replica), graceful drain on shutdown (`lifecycle`), and ArgoCD or Helm hooks for the migrations job (`migrationJob.hooks.*`, see Helm PreSync hooks).

content.text:
I have everything I need. Here's the complete plan.

---

# LiteLLM Proxy over ChatGPT Plus (Codex OAuth) — Implementation Plan

## 0. Key research findings that shape the design

1. **What LiteLLM actually bridges.** The `chatgpt/*` provider does **not** bridge ChatGPT's web app — it bridges **Codex** (`chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex`). It authenticates with your **ChatGPT plan** through OAuth **device-code flow**, using the plan's entitlement, **no OpenAI API billing**.
2. **Token file, not API key.** Auth is a token file (`auth.json`) written to `CHATGPT_TOKEN_DIR`/`CHATGPT_AUTH_FILE` on first login. LiteLLM **auto-refreshes** tokens in place via the OAuth refresh grant. This is exactly what lets a **single replica + a PersistentVolume** survive restarts/redeploys **without re-authentication** — matching the acceptance criterion and your chosen shape.
3. **Proxy non-interactive mode.** PR #24983 added `chatgpt_auth_file_path` per deployment: when an explicit path is set, interactive device-login is disabled so the pod won't block/hang on startup waiting for a browser. We will use this.
4. **Endpoints.** `/v1/responses` is **native**; `/v1/chat/completions` is **bridged** (`mode: responses`), blocked token-limit fields are stripped, and non-streaming completions are aggregated server-side. Codex model quality is fully supported.
5. **Model entitlement (critical).** Confirmed via a live report: `gpt-5.4-pro` (and Pro-only models) **error out on a ChatGPT account** — *"not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account"*. Prox5/Pro models MUST NOT be seeded. ChatGPT **Plus** → **GPT-5.6** (Terra/Sol/Luna/Instant) + Codex, and `gpt-5.4`/`gpt-5.3-codex` (the latter deprecated in Codex). We seed a conservative, later-verified set (verify-then-configure, per your answer).
6. **Chart footguns.** The Helm chart's default `image.tag` renders `main-<version>` which **does not exist** on ghcr → `ImagePullBackOff`. **We must set `image.tag` explicitly** to a published tag. Community chart, frequent releases.
7. **Cloudflare challenge risk.** Multiple 2026 reports: the Codex `/chat/completions` path sometimes returns a Cloudflare HTML challenge if no cookie is present. `/v1/responses` is the reliable path. This is a reported upstream gap we'll document + work around (route via responses), not fix.
8. **Cluster conventions** (audited): Traefik-only ingress, `cloudflare` DNS-01 resolver, namespace-local `security-headers` middleware, `local-path` storage pinned to s145 for stateful workloads. Flux-managed apps live in `anywhere/k8s/<app>/` + a Kustomization in `clusters/s145/`, encrypted secrets via `.sops.yaml` + `decryption: sops` on the Kustomization.

---

## 1. Architecture

```
 clients (Cursor/OpenCode/openai SDK)
   │  base_url=https://litellm.beijns.eu.org   (TLS, gated by gateway API key)
   ▼
 Traefik IngressRoute (websecure, certResolver=cloudflare, security-headers)
   ▼
 litellm-helm Deployment (replicas=1, nodeSelector s145)
   ├─ config.yaml via configMapGenerator (proxy_config / values)
   ├─ LITELLM_MASTER_KEY  (Secret from SOPS)
   ├─ Postgres (virtual keys, master-key UI persistence) — local-path PVC on s145
   └─ CHATGPT_TOKEN_DIR → PersistentVolume (auth.json, writable for token refresh)
                 │
   chatgpt/* provider (device-flow token, auto-refresh)
   │  └─ https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex  (egress from s145, plain internet)
   ▼
 /v1/responses (native)   /v1/chat/completions (bridged → responses)

- Persistence: `auth.json` on a dedicated PVC so a pod restart/redeploy reuses the cached token and refresh grant → **no re-auth** until upstream expiry/revocation.
- Two PVCs, both `local-path` pinned to s145: `litellm-db` (Postgres) and `litellm-tokens` (OAuth auth.json, ReadWriteOnce, single replica).
```

Key files (mirroring your proven `immich` pattern):

```
anywhere/clusters/s145/litellm.yaml              # Flux Kustomization (sops decrypt, dependsOn infra)
anywhere/k8s/litellm/
├── kustomization.yaml      # resources + configMapGenerator(proxy-config ← config.yaml)
├── namespace.yaml          # namespace: litellm
├── helmrepository.yaml     # OCI ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-helm
├── litellm-helm.yaml       # HelmRelease (pinned tag, replicaCount 1, s145, env)
├── config.yaml             # model_list + litellm_settings (source for ConfigMap)
├── litellm-secret.yaml     # SOPS-encrypted (LITELLM_MASTER_KEY, CHATGPT_TOKEN_DIR)
├── database.yaml           # Postgres Deployment+Service+PVC (or chart-deployStandalone)
├── token-pvc.yaml          # PVC for auth.json (+ init/login Job manifest)
├── security-headers.yaml   # namespaced Traefik middleware
└── ingressroute.yaml       # Host(litellm.beijns.eu.org)
```

---

## 2. Deployment values (`litellm-helm.yaml` + `values.yaml`)

```
replicaCount: 1
image:
  repository: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent (or Always for rollback precision)
  tag: "<pin, e.g. v1.90.2>"     # MUST be explicit — avoid main-<tag> ImagePullBackOff
numWorkers: 1
nodeSelector: { kubernetes.io/hostname: s145 }
masterkeySecretName: litellm-secret
masterkeySecretKey: LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
proxyConfigMap: { create: true }   # renders config.yaml from values.proxy_config
db:
  useExisting: true
  deployStandalone: false
  endpointUrl: postgres internally (litellm-postgres.litellm.svc.cluster.local:5432)
  database: litellm
  secret: {name/litellm/DB creds}
persistence:
  tokenDir: { capacity: 1Gi, storageClassName: local-path }  # auth.json durable, writable by pod
environmentFrom / extraEnv:
  - CHATGPT_TOKEN_DIR=/data/chatgpt
  - CHATGPT_AUTH_FILE=auth.json
  - LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=...

pg-supers: keep Postgres in-namespace pinned to s145 w/ its own PVC (mirror immich pattern).
```

> If we prefer to avoid a separate Postgres manifest, we can instead set `db.deployStandalone: true` (chart bundles Bitnami Postgres). Decision: I'll default to **in-namespace standalone Postgres via chart** for a single sealed unit, PVC-backed on s145, and revisit if we want a shared DB.

---

## 3. Model & gateway config (`proxy_config` → `config.yaml`)

```yaml
model_list:
  # Responses-native, Codex + ChatGPT Plus entitlement (prox-less):
  - model_name: chatgpt-codex            # alias clients call
    model_info: { mode: responses }
    litellm_params:
      model: chatgpt/gpt-5.4-codex       # verify at runtime; fall back to gpt-5.3-codex / gpt-5.6-*
      chatgpt_auth_file_path: /data/chatgpt/auth.json
  - model_name: chatgpt-mini
    model_info: { mode: responses }
    litellm_params:
      model: chatgpt/gpt-5.4-mini
      chatgpt_auth_file_path: /data/chatgpt/auth.json
  # add gpt-5.6-* entries only after the login proves they resolve (verify-then-configure)

# bridge: route openai-based chat completions through responses
litellm_settings:
  route_all_chat_openai_to_responses: true
  drop_params: true

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
```

- **Do not** register `gpt-5.4-pro` / any Pro model (rejected on ChatGPT account).
- Seed only a small verified set; after the device login, hit `/v1/models`/upstream and prune anything that errors.
- Optionally add a second model backed by a **paid provider** (OpenRouter/local) as a resilience fallback — I'll flag this as a recommendation, not required.

---

## 4. Secrets & persistence design

| Secret | Source | Notes |
|--------|--------|-------|
| `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` | `litellm-secret.yaml` (SOPS) | Master key → create **virtual keys** for each client; only `sk-...` virtual keys handed out. Never the ChatGPT token. |
| OAuth `auth.json` | **PVC, not a Secret/ConfigMap** | Must be **writable** (token refresh) so can't be a static Secret. Written once via `litellm-chatgpt-login` device flow into the mounted token PVC. Revocable by deleting the file. |
| Postgres creds | `database-secret.yaml` (SOPS) | image-scoped. |

- `.sops.yaml` creation rule: `k8s/litellm/*-secret.yaml` → recipients `pro_darwin`, `mark`, `s145_cluster`, `encrypted_regex: ^(data|stringData)$`, then `sops updatekeys`.
- Ensure `Secret/flux-system/sops-age` exists (documented requirement for Flux decrypt). 

---

## 5. Controlled ChatGPT Plus device-authentication procedure

One-time, human-gated, from the **operator machine** (matches "controlled procedure"):
1. Chart + PVCs deployed first (dry run).
2. Launch the device login against the mounted token PVC. Simplest, non-intrusive:
   ```bash
   kubectl -n litellm run chatgpt-login --rm -it --image=ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database:<pin> \
     --overrides='{"spec":{"nodeSelector":{"kubernetes.io/hostname":"s145"},"volumes":[{"name":"tok","persistentVolumeClaim":{"claimName":"litellm-token"}}],"containers":[{"name":"c","image":"...","stdin":true,"command":["/bin/sh","-c","CHATGPT_TOKEN_DIR=/data/chatgpt litellm-chatgpt-login && sleep 5"],"volumeMounts":[{"name":"tok","mountPath":"/data/chatgpt"}]}]}}'
   ```
   (or a dedicated tracked **Job** we commit under `k8s/litellm/login-job.yaml`). Operator completes device code in the browser.
3. `litellm-chatgpt-login` writes `auth.json` into `/data/chatgpt` on the PVC.
4. Confirm the file exists (`kubectl -n litellm exec ... cat /data/chatgpt/auth.json`), then **delete the login Job/pod**; the main Deployment's `config.yaml` points `chatgpt_auth_file_path` at that file.
5. LiteLLM now loads the token on every start; auto-refresh in place. **No re-login on restart** until expiry/revocation.

> This is the controlled, non-interactive-safe sequence (per `chatgpt_auth_file_path` behavior in PF #32602).

---

## 6. Exposure (IngressRoute) — private + TLS

```yaml
apiVersion: traefik.io/v1alpha1
kind: IngressRoute
metadata: { name: litellm, namespace: litellm }
spec:
  entryPoints: [websecure]
  routes:
    - match: Host(`litellm.beijns.eu.org`)
      kind: Rule
      middlewares:
        - name: security-headers        # namespace-local copy
      services:
        - name: litellm                # Service → 4000
          port: 4000
  tls:
    certResolver: cloudflare
    domains: [ { main: litellm.beijns.eu.org } ]
```
- DNS CNAME `litellm.beijns.eu.org` → proxied in Cloudflare; cert via existing `cloudflare` DNS-01 resolver.
- Note: subdomain is public-DNS but **every API call requires a LiteLLM virtual key + TLS**; the dashboard is admin-gated. This satisfies "not publicly accessible without auth + transport security." Provide Traefik to also restrict dashboard (`.path /admin` requiring a header) — optional. The subdomain being internet-reachable is intentional so external dev clients work; **keys** are the gate.

---

## 7. Health, readiness & persistence verification

- Readiness/`/health/liveliness` and `readiness` — set Deployment probes (`livenessProbe/readinessProbe` on port 4000 path `/health/liveliness` and `/health/readiness`) so the pod doesn't serve traffic before the OAuth token is loaded. **Critical** to prevent "restart loop"/serving-401 window.
- Persistence checks: `kubectl -n litellm get pvc` shows Bound; after forced restart (`kubectl rollout restart`), assert `/data/chatgpt/auth.json` still exists and `/v1/models` still lists aliases (i.e., no re-login).
- Postgres `Ready` before deployment goes live (use `dependsOn`/init-wait or readiness).

---

## 8. Endpoint verification checklist

```bash
# health/readiness
curl -s https://litellm.beijns.eu/health/liveliness  -H "authorization: Bearer $KEY"

# /v1/models → returns our aliases
curl -s https://litellm.beijns.eu/v1/models           -H "authorization: Bearer $KEY"  | jq .data[].id

# /v1/responses (codex family — native, the acceptance path)
curl -s https://litellm.beijns.eu/v1/responses \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"chatgpt-codex","input":"Say hello"}'

# /v1/chat/completions (bridged → responses)
curl -s https://litellm.beijns.eu/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"chatgpt-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}]}'

# unauthorized → must be 401/403
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://litellm.beijns.eu/v1/models
```
Acceptance mapping is documented in §12.

---

## 9. Example client configs

**OpenCode / OpenAI SDK (generic):**
```python
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI(base_url="https://litellm.beijns.eu", api_key="sk-litellm-client-key")
r = client.responses.create(model="chatgpt-codex", input="hi")
```

**Cursor/appset** (OpenAI-compatible): base URL `https://litellm.beijns.eu`, API key = the LiteLLM virtual key, model `chatgpt-codex`.

---

## 10. Troubleshooting guide

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|--------|--------------|-----|
| HTTP 401/403 to proxy | missing/wrong virtual key; sub-status | create virtual key via `/key/generate` with LITELLM_MASTER_KEY; check `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` secret |
| HTTP 400 model "not supported for ChatGPT account" | seeded a Prox model | remove `gpt-5.4-pro`/`*-pro` entries; verify with `GET /v1/models`/upstream |
| Cloudflare HTML / "Enable JavaScript" | /chat_completions challenge (known upstream) | use `/v1/responses`; the default; route chat→responses (done) |
| empty `output: []` after completion | known LiteLLM ChatGPT aggregation gap (older PR #25429-ish) | pin newer release; retry; stream=true |
| pod "restart loop for device code | proxy blocking startup waiting for interactive login | ensure `chatgpt_auth_file_path` set (disables interactive), token PVC mounted/pre-warmed |
| `ImagePullBackOff` at install | chart default `main-<ver` missing | pin `image.tag` to published tag (e.g. `v1.90.2`) |
| gpt-5.4-family errors in Aug | models retiring from Codex (Aug 31 2026) | migrate aliases to gpt-5.6-* (terra/luna/sol); verify entitlement |
| egress blocked | chatgpt.com unreachable from s145/Cloudflare geo | confirm pods can reach `chatgpt.com:443`; check CF WAF/geo; try alternative resolver/egress |

---

## 11. Rollback & credential revocation

- **Rollback image**: since `image.tag` is pinned and `deployment.yaml` uses immutable image, redeploy previous tag → restore, and to roll config, `flux reconcile` back to a prior commit or `helm rollback`.
- **Revoke access**: delete the `auth.json` (or the whole `litellm-token` PVC) → forces full re-login; also replace the ChatGPT account password/`logout` current sessions under OpenAI security settings; delete virtual keys via admin API (`/key/delete`) to cut client access instantly.
- **Rotate master key**: update SOPS `litellm-secret` and re-sync.

---

## 12. Verified vs assumed (explicit)

- **Verified (from docs/releases, May–Aug 2026):** `chatgpt/*` = Codex via device-flow; native `/responses`, bridged `/chat/completions`; filesystem token auto-refresh; `chatgpt_auth_file_path` disables interactive login; Pro models refused on ChatGPT accounts; chart needs `image.tag`/ImagePullBackOff; `gpt-5.4`/`gpt-5.4-mini` retire from Codex 2026-08-31.
- **Assumed / to confirm at build:** exact GPT-5.6 model strings LiteLLM accepts, and whether Plus's full 5.6 fleet resolves when proxied — verified **after first login** and pruned before going live. The Cloudflare-challenge-on-`/chat/completions` and empty-output issues are community-reported and may vary by IP/region; our primary path is `/v1/responses`.

---

## 13. Suggested execution order

1. `.sops.yaml` rule + `sops updatekeys`; SOPS secrets (`litellm-secret`, `postgres-secret`).
2. Author `k8s/litellm/*` (namespace, helmrepo, helmrelease+values, database, PSC token PVC, ingressroute, security-headers, Kustomization); `k8s/clusters/s145/litellm.yaml`.
3. Rule `flux reconcile kustomization litellm -n flux-system --with-source`.
4. Device-login Job → operator completes Codey+ → confment; verify `/v1/models`.
5. Fill virtual keys, run endpoint verification suite, then hand out configs to Cursor/generic SDK. Client/churn.

---

The plan is complete. It matches your `k8s/*` conventions (Flux + SOPS + Traefik + s145-pinned local-path), pins images, and explicitly separates verified behavior from community/assumed behavior. Title: [Fix] Docker: Pin Wolfi And Uv To Multi-Arch Index Digests
URL: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/27123
Published: N/A
Author: N/A
Highlights:
Pin `wolfi-base` and `uv` to their **multi-arch image-index** digests in `Dockerfile`, `docker/Dockerfile.database`, and `docker/Dockerfile.non_root`.
...
The previous pins resolved to **single-platform amd64** manifests, not the OCI index. When buildx was asked to build for `linux/amd64,linux/arm64`, it pulled the same amd64 base for both targets, and the published image index advertised an `arm64` entry whose layers were byte-identical to the `amd64` entry. Effect for users: `docker pull --platform=linux/arm64 ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.83.14-stable` got them an amd64 binary.
...
Replace the per-platform digests with the corresponding image-index digests:
...
| Image | Old (per-platform amd64) | New (image index) |
|---|---|---|
| `cgr.dev/chainguard/wolfi-base` | `sha256:f26d42a15d09…` | `sha256:3258be472764337fd13095bcbb3182da170243b5819fd67ad4c0754590588b31` |
| `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.11.7` | `sha256:733b40421877…` | `sha256:240fb85ab0f263ef12f492d8476aa3a2e4e1e333f7d67fbdd923d00a506a516a` |
...
Both digests came from `docker buildx imagetools inspect `, which returns the **image-index** digest (multi-arch). For comparison, `docker pull` + `docker inspect` returns the **per-platform** digest of whatever platform the host pulled, which is how the broken pins slipped in.
...
{{.Manifest.Digest}}
...
sha256
...
3258be472764337fd13095bcbb3182da170243b5819fd67ad4c0754590588b31

$ docker buildx imagetools inspect cgr.dev/chainguard/wolfi-base:latest | grep Platform
  Platform:  linux/amd64
  Platform:  linux/arm64
...
$ docker buildx imagetools inspect ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.11.7 --format '{{.Manifest.Digest}}'
sha256:240fb85ab0f263ef12f492d8476aa3a2e4e1e333f7d67fbdd923d00a506a516a

$ docker buildx imagetools inspect ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.11.7 | grep Platform
  Platform:    linux/amd64
  Platform:    unknown/unknown   (attestation manifest)
  Platform:    linux/arm64
  Platform:    unknown/unknown   (attestation manifest)
```
...
The `mediaType` of each new digest is `application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json`, the per-platform manifests it contains are accessible at `cgr.dev/v2/chainguard/wolfi-base/manifests/sha256:3258be47…` and `ghcr.io/v2/astral-sh/uv/manifests/sha256:240fb85a…` respectively (verified directly via the registry API).
...

- [ ] `docker run --platform=linux/amd64 uname -m` returns `x86_64`.
- [ ] All three variants (`litellm`, `litellm-database`, `litellm-non_root`) verified.

...
LiteLLM now supports the GPT-5.6 family. Route traffic to OpenAI's newest frontier models through the LiteLLM AI Gateway with no code changes.
...
GPT-5.6 introduces a new naming system where the number identifies the generation and the tier name identifies a durable capability level.`gpt-5.6-sol` is the flagship for complex reasoning and agentic workloads,`gpt-5.6-terra` is a balanced model for everyday work with performance competitive with GPT-5.5 at roughly half the cost, and`gpt-5.6-luna` is the fastest and most affordable tier. Per OpenAI, the family sets a new state of the art on agentic coding (Terminal-Bench 2.1) with broad gains in long-horizon biology and cybersecurity workflows. GPT-5.6 also adds a new`max` reasoning effort for the deepest single-agent thinking and an`ultra` mode that coordinates subagents on the most complex tasks.
...
This post is updated as GPT-5.6 support expands. GPT-5.6 is now available on Azure OpenAI in addition to OpenAI direct. Global Azure deployments match OpenAI list pricing, and regional deployments (`azure/us/*` and`azure/eu/*`) are tracked with the standard 10% regional uplift.
...
No Docker image upgrade needed. GPT-5.6 routes through the existing`OpenAIGPT5Config` in LiteLLM (the version classifier already matches`gpt-5.4` and newer), so any recent version works out of the box. The GPT-5.6 pricing and metadata are also bundled starting in`v1.93.0-dev.2` for anyone running with`LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=true`.

Research and cluster-convention audit complete. All open decisions are resolved; here is the final plan.

---

# LiteLLM Proxy (ChatGPT Plus OAuth) on `oracle-eu-arm1` — Implementation Plan

## 0. Decisions locked in (from your answers + verified facts)

| Decision | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Node | `oracle-eu-arm1` (A1.Flex, **aarch64**, non-micro) | Your explicit choice. Pod + PVC pinned here via `nodeSelector`/`local-path`. |
| Image | `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.94.0` — **pinned, no `latest`** | arm64 manifests exist on ghcr (Docker Hub is amd64-only). v1.94.0 verified end-to-end by a community validator against a real ChatGPT sub with `gpt-5.6-*`. |
| Delivery | **Plain kustomize manifests, manually applied** (like `vaultwarden`) | `litellm-helm` exists but is community-maintained, bundles Postgres/Redis/autoscaling/PDB we don't need, and its default `image.tag` (`main-<ver>`) is a known `ImagePullBackOff` bug. For 1 replica, 2 models, no public route — manifests win. |
| Exposure | **NodePort only; no IngressRoute, no public DNS** | Clients on the Tailnet reach `http://100.84.230.4:<nodePort>`. WireGuard encrypts tailnet traffic = transport security. |
| Secrets | Random creds, SOPS-encrypted to **`mark` + `pro_darwin`** only | Your explicit instruction. Mirrors the IaC pattern. Because of this, the app is **not** Flux-managed (Flux decrypts with `s145_cluster`, which this file deliberately excludes). |
| Models | `gpt-5.6-sol` (aliased) + `gpt-5.3-codex` | Your explicit choice. Both are valid `chatgpt/*` subscription aliases. No Pro models. |

---

## 1. What we deploy (final shape)

```
anywhere/k8s/litellm/
├── kustomization.yaml      # resources list (no secret here)
├── namespace.yaml          # namespace: litellm
├── config.yaml             # model_list + litellm_settings (→ ConfigMap, no secrets)
├── deployment.yaml         # replicas=1, nodeSelector oracle-eu-arm1, envFrom litellm-secret,
│                           #   mounts token PVC, probes on /health/liveliness + /health/readiness
├── service.yaml            # NodePort 31400 → 4000, externalTrafficPolicy: Local
├── pvc.yaml                # local-path, 1Gi, pinned to oracle-eu-arm1 (auth.json + sqlite db)
└── secret.enc.yaml         # SOPS-encrypted (mark + pro_darwin) — LITELLM_MASTER_KEY, LITELLM_SALT_KEY
└── README.md               # runbook: apply, login, rotate, revoke
```

**Why NodePort + no route:** cluster is single k3s rooted at s145; `nodeSelector: kubernetes.io/hostname: oracle-eu-arm1` keeps everything on the ARM node; `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` + the pod's NodePort means only the running pod's node serves it. `100.84.230.4:31400` is the client base URL over Tailscale.

### `config.yaml` (key part)
```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: chatgpt-sol            # alias clients use
    model_info:
      mode: responses
      max_input_tokens: 1050000        # required: chatgpt/* metadata can report null otherwise
      max_output_tokens: 128000
    litellm_params:
      model: chatgpt/gpt-5.6-sol
      chatgpt_auth_file_path: /data/chatgpt/auth.json   # disables interactive login; fails fast
  - model_name: chatgpt-codex
    model_info:
      mode: responses
    litellm_params:
      model: chatgpt/gpt-5.3-codex
      chatgpt_auth_file_path: /data/chatgpt/auth.json

litellm_settings:
  drop_params: true
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  salt_key: os.environ/LITELLM_SALT_KEY
```
- `chatgpt_auth_file_path` (PR #24983) prevents the startup "device-code restart loop" and makes the pod non-interactive.
- Explicit token limits on `gpt-5.6-sol` — community-verified fix for `max_input_tokens: null` breaking long sessions.
- `route_all_chat_openai_to_responses` not needed; both models are already `mode: responses`.

### `secret.enc.yaml` (SOPS, mark + pro_darwin only)
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata: { name: litellm-secret, namespace: litellm }
type: Opaque
stringData:
  LITELLM_MASTER_KEY: <openssl rand -base64 48>
  LITELLM_SALT_KEY:    <openssl rand -base64 32>
```
- **Generate**: `openssl rand -base64 48` (master), `openssl rand -base64 32` (salt). Random, never committed plaintext.
- **New `.sops.yaml` creation rule**:
  ```yaml
  - path_regex: k8s/litellm/secret.enc.yaml
    encrypted_regex: "^(data|stringData)$"
    key_groups:
      - age: [*pro_darwin, *mark]      # NO s145_cluster — per your instruction
  ```
  → `sops updatekeys -y anywhere/k8s/litellm/secret.enc.yaml`.
- **Apply flow** (manual, keeps it out of Flux):
  ```bash
  export SOPS_AGE_KEY_FILE="$HOME/.config/sops/age/keys.txt"
  sops -d anywhere/k8s/litellm/secret.enc.yaml | kubectl apply -f -
  kubectl kustomize anywhere/k8s/litellm | kubectl apply -f -
  ```
  `config.yaml` → `configMapGenerator`; deployment `envFrom: litellm-secret`.

### PVC
- `local-path`, `1Gi`, `nodeSelector` pin, mounts at `/data/chatgpt`. Holds `auth.json` (writable — token refresh) and the local sqlite key store. Survives restarts; **no re-auth on pod restart** until upstream expiry/revocation.

---

## 2. Deployment env / health

```yaml
env:
  - { name: CHATGPT_TOKEN_DIR, value: /data/chatgpt }
  - { name: CHATGPT_AUTH_FILE, value: auth.json }
  - { name: STORE_MODEL_IN_DB, value: "false" }   # keep model config from ConfigMap
envFrom: [ { secretRef: { name: litellm-secret } } ]
livenessProbe:  { httpGet: { path: /health/liveliness, port: 4000 } }
readinessProbe: { httpGet: { path: /health/readiness, port: 4000 } }
nodeSelector: { kubernetes.io/hostname: oracle-eu-arm1 }
```
- Pre-flight before apply: `docker manifest inspect ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.94.0 --platform linux/arm64` to confirm the arm64 tag exists (research shows multi-arch on ghcr, verify anyway).
- If the plain image errors on DB at startup, swap to `litellm-database:v1.94.0` (same version, bundles Prisma) — flagged as fallback, not expected.

---

## 3. One-time ChatGPT device login (controlled procedure)

1. Deploy manifests (dry pod comes up healthy; readiness may be red until auth exists — expected).
2. Run a one-off login Job (manifests committed) that mounts the same PVC and runs:
   ```
   image: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.94.0
   command: litellm-chatgpt-login
   env:    CHATGPT_TOKEN_DIR=/data/chatgpt
   volumes: [ { name: tok, persistentVolumeClaim: { claimName: litellm-token } } ]
   ```
3. `kubectl -n litellm logs -f <login-pod>` → prints a **device code + verification URL**.
4. You complete the flow in the browser (sign in with the ChatGPT Plus account). CLI writes `auth.json` into the PVC at `/data/chatgpt/auth.json`.
5. Verify the file, delete the login Job, `kubectl rollout restart deploy/litellm` → pod picks up the token. No re-login on future restarts.

---

## 4. Verification checklist

```bash
# node reachability (Tailscale)
curl -sv http://100.84.230.4:31400/health/liveliness

# auth — unauthorized must be 401/403
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://100.84.230.4:31400/v1/models            # expect 401

# models → both aliases
curl -s http://100.84.230.4:31400/v1/models -H "authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" | jq .data[].id

# /v1/responses (native, Codex path)
curl -s http://100.84.230.4:31400/v1/responses -H "authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" -d '{"model":"chatgpt-sol","input":"Say hello"}'

# /v1/chat/completions (bridged)
curl -s http://100.84.230.4:31400/v1/chat/completions -H "authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"chatgpt-codex","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}]}'

# persistence: restart, confirm no re-auth
kubectl -n litellm rollout restart deploy/litellm
kubectl -n litellm exec deploy/litellm -- cat /data/chatgpt/auth.json   # still present
```

---

## 5. Client configs (all private, Tailnet)

- **OpenAI SDK / OpenCode**: `base_url=http://100.84.230.4:31400`, `api_key=<LITELLM_MASTER_KEY>`, model `chatgpt-sol`.
- **Cursor**: custom OpenAI provider → same base URL, key, model `chatgpt-sol`.
- Create a dedicated virtual key via `/key/generate` (master-key authed) for each client instead of sharing the master key, if desired.

---

## 6. Rollback & credential revocation

- **App rollback**: `kubectl -n litellm rollout undo deploy/litellm` (image is pinned+immutable) or `kubectl apply` a prior commit.
- **Revoke ChatGPT access**: delete the PVC (`litellm-token`) → forces full re-login; additionally revoke sessions / change password in OpenAI account security. Delete the master key secret to cut all client access instantly.
- **Rotate keys**: regenerate, re-`sops -e`, re-apply; rollout restart.

---

## 7. Verified vs assumed (explicit)

- **Verified (docs/PRs/GH, 2026):** `chatgpt/*` = Codex via device-flow; `gpt-5.6-sol` + `gpt-5.3-codex` are valid subscription aliases; `chatgpt_auth_file_path` disables interactive login; Pro models rejected on ChatGPT accounts; ghcr images are multi-arch (arm64 OK); chart default tag bug → we pin; `gpt-5.6-*` needs explicit token limits; `gpt-5.4`/`gpt-5.3-codex` deprecated in Codex CLI but still served via subscription OAuth.
- **Assumed / verify at apply:** exact `v1.94.0` arm64 manifest exists; sqlite-local mode on the plain image (fallback `litellm-database`); NodePort reachable on the tailnet interface (if the host firewall blocks it, add a NixOS `openFirewallRules`/Tailscale-trusted-interface rule on `oracle-eu-arm1`); `gpt-5.3-codex` returns output on the subscription OAuth path (some community reports of empty output — primary path is `/v1/responses`).

---

Ready to execute when you switch out of plan mode. First step will be the SOPS rule + secret generation (`openssl rand`), then the manifests, then the guided device login.

# Production Deployment

Production deployment guide for AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, or any Kubernetes cluster. For a first deployment on a single machine, start with the [Quickstart](/docs/proxy/docker_quick_start); this page picks up where it ends.

There are two supported paths. If you run Kubernetes, [deploy with Helm](#deploy-with-helm) on EKS, GKE, or AKS; the install is the same on every cloud, only the data stores and ingress differ. If you do not run Kubernetes, AWS and GCP have [official Terraform modules](#deploy-with-terraform-aws-and-gcp) that stand up the entire stack; Azure has no Terraform module, so AKS with Helm is the supported path there.

## Architecture[​](#architecture "Direct link to Architecture")

![](/img/cloud_icons/aws.svg)AWS![](/img/cloud_icons/google-cloud.svg)Google Cloud![](/img/cloud_icons/microsoft-azure.svg)Azure

Terraform on ECS FargateEKS with HelmEKS with Helm (microservices)

Clients (OpenAI SDK, LangChain, curl)

![](/img/cloud_icons/aws-elb.svg)

Application Load BalancerHTTPS, path-based routing

![](/img/cloud_icons/aws-ecs.svg)

ECS Fargategateway :4000, backend :4001, ui :3000

gatewaybackendui

![](/img/cloud_icons/aws-rds.svg)

Aurora PostgreSQLwriter + reader, IAM auth

![](/img/cloud_icons/aws-elasticache.svg)

ElastiCache Redismulti-AZ, TLS

![](/img/cloud_icons/aws-secrets-manager.svg)

Secrets Managermaster key, provider keys

LiteLLM provides two deployment modes:

-   **Monolithic**: one `litellm` image serves LLM traffic, management APIs, and the UI. This is what the `litellm-helm` chart runs, and the simplest to operate.
-   **Microservices**: a `gateway` (LLM traffic, port 4000), `backend` (management APIs and UI backend, port 4001), and `ui` (port 3000), each deployed and scaled independently. This is what the componentized `litellm` chart and both Terraform modules run; see the [chart values](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/main/helm/litellm/values.yaml) for the full reference.

The supporting infrastructure is identical in either mode:

Component

Purpose

Notes

LiteLLM services

One proxy deployment (monolithic) or gateway + backend + ui (microservices)

Stateless; run 2+ replicas behind a load balancer

PostgreSQL

Keys, teams, users, spend logs, config

Required for the proxy's auth and tracking features

Redis

Rate limiting, router state, caching across instances

Required once you run more than one instance

Migrations job

Applies schema migrations against Postgres

Runs once per upgrade; proxy instances set `DISABLE_SCHEMA_UPDATE=true`

## Core configuration[​](#core-configuration "Direct link to Core configuration")

```
DATABASE_URL="REDACTED"LITELLM_MASTER_KEY="sk-..."   # admin key for the proxyLITELLM_SALT_KEY="sk-..."     # encrypts provider credentials stored in the DB. Set once, never change itDISABLE_SCHEMA_UPDATE="true"  # proxy instances never run migrations; the migrations job doesSTORE_MODEL_IN_DB="True"      # manage models from the Admin UI instead of config files
```

`LITELLM_SALT_KEY` cannot be rotated after you add models: it encrypts the provider credentials stored in your database, and changing it makes them unreadable. Generate a strong random value and store both keys in your cloud's secret manager.

Official images are published to `ghcr.io/berriai` and mirrored at `docker.litellm.ai/berriai`. Use `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database` for monolithic deployments with Postgres (it bundles the Prisma toolchain), and pin a version tag rather than `latest` or a moving tag, so rollbacks are deterministic. All images are signed; see the [Docker Image Security Guide](/docs/proxy/docker_image_security) for verification and the non-root variant.

## Provision the data stores[​](#provision-the-data-stores "Direct link to Provision the data stores")

The Helm path needs a PostgreSQL database and a Redis reachable from your cluster. Use the managed services:

-   AWS
-   Google Cloud
-   Azure

Provision [RDS PostgreSQL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_PostgreSQL.html) and [ElastiCache Redis](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/WhatIs.html) in the same VPC as your EKS cluster, with security groups permitting the cluster's nodes on ports 5432 and 6379.

Provision [Cloud SQL PostgreSQL](https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres) and [Memorystore Redis](https://cloud.google.com/memorystore/docs/redis) with private IPs on the VPC your GKE cluster uses (Cloud SQL needs [Private Services Access](https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/private-services-access)). Use the instances' private IPs as the endpoints below.

```
az group create --name litellm-prod --location eastusaz aks create --resource-group litellm-prod --name litellm-aks \  --node-count 3 --enable-managed-identityaz postgres flexible-server create --resource-group litellm-prod \  --name litellm-db --database-name litellm \  --tier GeneralPurpose --sku-name Standard_D2ds_v5az redis create --resource-group litellm-prod --name litellm-redis \  --location eastus --sku Standard --vm-size c1
```

Docs: [AKS](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/what-is-aks), [Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/postgresql/flexible-server/overview), [Azure Cache for Redis](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-cache-for-redis/cache-overview). Azure Cache for Redis serves TLS on port 6380, and TLS is enabled through the URL scheme: instead of `redis_host` and `redis_port`, set `redis_url: "rediss://:<access-key>@litellm-redis.redis.cache.windows.net:6380"` under `router_settings` (the `rediss://` scheme turns TLS on).

## Deploy with Helm[​](#deploy-with-helm "Direct link to Deploy with Helm")

First create the secrets both charts consume:

```
kubectl create secret generic litellm-masterkey \  --from-literal=masterkey="sk-$(openssl rand -hex 24)"kubectl create secret generic litellm-db \  --from-literal=username=litellm \  --from-literal=password="<database-password>"kubectl create secret generic litellm-env \  --from-literal=LITELLM_SALT_KEY="sk-$(openssl rand -hex 24)" \  --from-literal=REDIS_PASSWORD="<redis-password>" \  --from-literal=OPENAI_API_KEY="<provider-key>"
```

Then pick a deployment mode:

-   Monolithic (litellm-helm)
-   Microservices (litellm)

values.yaml

```
replicaCount: 3image:  repository: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database  tag: "v1.90.2"          # pin your versionmasterkeySecretName: litellm-masterkeymasterkeySecretKey: masterkeydb:  useExisting: true  deployStandalone: false  endpoint: "<postgres-endpoint>"  database: litellm  secret:    name: litellm-db    usernameKey: username    passwordKey: passwordenvironmentSecrets:  - litellm-envproxy_config:  model_list:    - model_name: gpt-4o      litellm_params:        model: openai/gpt-4o        api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY  router_settings:    redis_host: "<redis-endpoint>"    redis_port: 6379    redis_password: os.environ/REDIS_PASSWORD
```

```
helm install litellm oci://ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-helm -f values.yaml
```

The chart lives at [`helm/litellm-helm`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/main/helm/litellm-helm); the published chart versions carry LiteLLM release numbers (for example `1.90.2`), and `helm show values oci://ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-helm` lists every knob. Beyond the values above it supports [autoscaling](#autoscaling) (`autoscaling.*` or `keda.*`), PodDisruptionBudgets (`pdb.*`), a Prometheus ServiceMonitor (`serviceMonitor.*`), read replica routing (`db.readReplicaUrl`, see [Database Read Replica](/docs/proxy/db_read_replica)), graceful drain on shutdown (`lifecycle`), and ArgoCD or Helm hooks for the migrations job (`migrationJob.hooks.*`, see [Helm PreSync hooks](/docs/proxy/prod#run-migrations-from-the-helm-presync-hook)).

values.yaml

```
masterKey:  secretName: litellm-masterkey  secretKey: masterkeydatabase:  writer:    host: "<postgres-endpoint>"    port: 5432    dbname: litellm    passwordSecret:      name: litellm-db      usernameKey: username      passwordKey: password  # optional: add database.reader to route reads to a replicaredis:  host: "<redis-endpoint>"  port: 6379  passwordSecret:    name: litellm-env    passwordKey: REDIS_PASSWORD# one host fronting gateway, backend, and uiingress:  enabled: true  className: "<alb | gce | azure-application-gateway>"  host: llm.example.com
```

```
helm upgrade --install litellm \  oci://ghcr.io/berriai/litellm/chart/litellm \  --version 1.89.2 \  -f values.yaml
```

This deploys `gateway`, `backend`, and `ui` as separate services with per-component autoscaling, so you can run many gateway replicas against a small fixed backend. It requires external Postgres and Redis (no bundled subcharts) and supports reader/writer database splits, IAM database auth, and Redis Cluster mode. Pin the chart to `1.89.0` or newer: the component images (`ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-gateway`, `-backend`, `-ui`, `-migrations`) are published to GHCR from `v1.89.0` onward, and each component's image tag defaults to the chart version, so older chart versions resolve to image tags that were never pushed. Every knob (per-component scaling and probes, read replica routing, Redis Cluster, migrations job, ingress) is documented in the [chart's values.yaml](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/main/helm/litellm/values.yaml); see [Autoscaling](#autoscaling) for the scaling blocks.

Both charts run the migrations job automatically and keep `DISABLE_SCHEMA_UPDATE=true` on the proxy pods. Expose the service through your cloud's ingress: the [AWS Load Balancer Controller](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/aws-load-balancer-controller.html) on EKS, [GKE Ingress](https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/ingress) on GKE, or [Application Gateway Ingress (AGIC)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/application-gateway/ingress-controller-overview) on AKS, with health checks on `/health/readiness`, then point your DNS record at the resulting load balancer. For secrets, prefer your cloud's secret manager over plain Kubernetes secrets ([Key Vault CSI driver](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/csi-secrets-store-driver) on AKS, for example); the charts consume whatever secret you mount.

### Autoscaling[​](#autoscaling "Direct link to Autoscaling")

Both charts can scale themselves, and both ship autoscaling off or conservative by default. For the thresholds to aim at, and why memory is not one of them, see [autoscaling in the production checklist](/docs/proxy/prod#autoscaling).

`litellm-helm` offers two mutually exclusive mechanisms. `autoscaling.*` renders a standard HorizontalPodAutoscaler, and `keda.*` renders a KEDA `ScaledObject` for scaling on queue depth, Prometheus queries, or anything else KEDA can read. Enabling both renders only the HPA, so pick one.

```
autoscaling:  enabled: false  minReplicas: 1  maxReplicas: 100  targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 80  # targetMemoryUtilizationPercentage and behavior are also acceptedkeda:  enabled: false  minReplicas: 1  maxReplicas: 100  pollingInterval: 30   # seconds between trigger evaluations  cooldownPeriod: 300   # seconds of quiet before scaling back to minReplicas  triggers: []          # required; a ScaledObject with no triggers will not scale
```

`keda.triggers` is empty by default and has no useful default, so supply the trigger yourself; the chart's `values.yaml` carries a commented Prometheus example. `keda.fallback`, `keda.behavior`, and `keda.restoreToOriginalReplicaCount` are passed through for controlling what happens when the metric source is unavailable and how replicas settle after a scale event.

The componentized chart scales each component on its own, under `gateway.hpa`, `backend.hpa`, and `ui.hpa`. The gateway and backend autoscale out of the box and the UI does not, with maximums sized to the shape of each component's traffic: the gateway defaults to `maxReplicas: 10` at 70 percent CPU and 80 percent memory, the backend to `maxReplicas: 4` at 70 percent CPU, and the UI to `maxReplicas: 3` at 80 percent CPU with `enabled: false`. Raising the gateway's ceiling is usually all you need, since it is the only component that sees LLM traffic.

Whichever mechanism you use, set the maximum against what your database can serve. The connection pool is per worker, so the ceiling on replicas is also a ceiling on Postgres connections; `litellm-helm` defaults `maxReplicas` to 100, which at the default pool limit of 10 asks for roughly 1000 connections at full scale-out. See [bounding database connections](/docs/proxy/prod#bound-database-connections).

### Kubernetes without Helm[​](#kubernetes-without-helm "Direct link to Kubernetes without Helm")

If you manage raw manifests, the equivalent deployment is a ConfigMap for `config.yaml`, a Secret for keys, a Deployment with health probes, and a Service.

Full manifest (ConfigMap, Secret, Deployment, Service)

```
apiVersion: v1kind: ConfigMapmetadata:  name: litellm-config-filedata:  config.yaml: |      model_list:        - model_name: gpt-4o          litellm_params:            model: openai/gpt-4o            api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY---apiVersion: v1kind: Secrettype: Opaquemetadata:  name: litellm-secretsdata:  OPENAI_API_KEY: REDACTED # your api key in base64---apiVersion: apps/v1kind: Deploymentmetadata:  name: litellm-deployment  labels:    app: litellmspec:  replicas: 2  selector:    matchLabels:      app: litellm  template:    metadata:      labels:        app: litellm    spec:      containers:      - name: litellm        image: docker.litellm.ai/berriai/litellm:v1.90.2 # pin a version, do not use :latest        args:          - "--config"          - "/app/proxy_server_config.yaml"        ports:        - containerPort: 4000        volumeMounts:        - name: config-volume          mountPath: /app/proxy_server_config.yaml          subPath: config.yaml        envFrom:        - secretRef:            name: litellm-secrets        livenessProbe:          httpGet:            path: /health/liveliness            port: 4000          initialDelaySeconds: 120          periodSeconds: 15        readinessProbe:          httpGet:            path: /health/readiness            port: 4000          initialDelaySeconds: 120          periodSeconds: 15      volumes:        - name: config-volume          configMap:            name: litellm-config-file---apiVersion: v1kind: Servicemetadata:  name: litellm-servicespec:  selector:    app: litellm  ports:    - protocol: TCP      port: 4000      targetPort: 4000  type: NodePort
```

To connect the database, switch the image to `docker.litellm.ai/berriai/litellm-database` and add `DATABASE_URL` and `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` to the Secret; nothing else in the manifest changes.

## Deploy with Terraform (AWS and GCP)[​](#deploy-with-terraform-aws-and-gcp "Direct link to Deploy with Terraform (AWS and GCP)")

The official modules deploy the full microservices stack (network, database, Redis, object storage, secrets, compute, load balancer, and a migrations job that runs before the services start) and are published to the Terraform Registry:

-   [`BerriAI/litellm/aws`](https://registry.terraform.io/modules/BerriAI/litellm/aws/latest)
-   [`BerriAI/litellm/google`](https://registry.terraform.io/modules/BerriAI/litellm/google/latest)

-   AWS (ECS Fargate)
-   Google Cloud (Cloud Run)

Provisions a VPC with public and private subnets, an Aurora PostgreSQL cluster (writer plus reader, IAM database auth), ElastiCache Redis (multi-AZ, encrypted), an S3 bucket, Secrets Manager entries, an Application Load Balancer, and ECS Fargate services.

main.tf

```
module "litellm" {  source  = "BerriAI/litellm/aws"  version = "~> 1.90"  region = "us-east-1"  azs    = ["us-east-1a", "us-east-1b"]  tenant = "acme"  env    = "prod"  ui_password         = var.ui_password  litellm_license     = var.litellm_license      # optional, omit for open source  acm_certificate_arn = var.acm_certificate_arn  # TLS is required by default  proxy_config = {    model_list = [{      model_name = "gpt-4o"      litellm_params = {        model   = "openai/gpt-4o"        api_key = "os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY"      }    }]  }  gateway_extra_secrets = {    OPENAI_API_KEY = var.openai_key_secret_arn  }}
```

Before you apply: provision the TLS certificate in [AWS Certificate Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/acm/latest/userguide/acm-overview.html) (the module refuses a plaintext ALB unless you explicitly set `allow_plaintext_alb = true`), and create any provider-key secrets in [Secrets Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/create_secret.html) first, since `gateway_extra_secrets` takes their ARNs. After apply, point your DNS record at the ALB hostname.

The module auto-generates the master key into Secrets Manager if you do not supply one. The application connects to Aurora with short-lived IAM tokens, so its `DATABASE_URL` carries no password (the database master password itself is generated into Secrets Manager and never touches the application). Every resource is named `<tenant>-litellm-<env>`, and the module declares no provider, so you can `for_each` it to run one stack per tenant.

Provisions a VPC with Private Services Access, Cloud SQL PostgreSQL (primary plus read replica), Memorystore Redis with TLS, a GCS bucket, Secret Manager entries, Cloud Run services, and a global HTTPS load balancer with serverless NEGs.

main.tf

```
module "litellm" {  source  = "BerriAI/litellm/google"  version = "~> 1.90"  project_id = "my-project"  region     = "us-central1"  tenant     = "acme"  env        = "prod"  ui_password     = var.ui_password  litellm_license = var.litellm_license  # optional  # Cloud Run cannot pull from ghcr.io. Point this at an Artifact Registry  # remote repository backed by ghcr.io, or mirror the images.  image_registry = "us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/my-project/ghcr-remote/berriai"  lb_domains = ["llm.example.com"]  proxy_config = {    model_list = [{      model_name = "gemini-2.5-pro"      litellm_params = { model = "vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-pro" }    }]  }}
```

Three GCP-specific caveats. First, always override `image_registry`: it defaults to `ghcr.io/berriai`, which Cloud Run cannot pull from, so the apply succeeds but the services fail at image pull. Point it at an [Artifact Registry remote repository](https://cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/repositories/remote-overview) that proxies `ghcr.io`. Second, the database uses password authentication through Secret Manager rather than IAM auth; LiteLLM's IAM token support is AWS RDS specific. Third, create the DNS record for `lb_domains` pointing at the load balancer IP after apply; the [Google-managed certificate](https://cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/ssl-certificates/google-managed-certs) will not finish provisioning until the domain resolves to it.

To manage LiteLLM resources (keys, teams, models) as code once the stack is up, use [terraform-provider-litellm](https://github.com/BerriAI/terraform-provider-litellm).

## Verify the deployment[​](#verify-the-deployment "Direct link to Verify the deployment")

Confirm the proxy is up and can reach its database:

```
curl -s https://llm.example.com/health/readiness
```

Then open the Admin UI at `https://llm.example.com/ui`, log in with your master key, add a model, create a virtual key, and send a Playground message; a response proves the full path through the load balancer, proxy, database, and provider credentials. # ChatGPT Subscription

Use ChatGPT Pro/Max subscription models through LiteLLM with OAuth device flow authentication.

Property

Details

Description

ChatGPT subscription access (Codex + GPT-5.3/5.4 family) via ChatGPT backend API

Provider Route on LiteLLM

`chatgpt/`

Supported Endpoints

`/responses`, `/chat/completions` (bridged to Responses for supported models)

API Reference

[https://chatgpt.com](https://chatgpt.com)

ChatGPT subscription access is native to the Responses API. Chat Completions requests are bridged to Responses for supported models (for example `chatgpt/gpt-5.4`).

Notes:

-   The ChatGPT subscription backend rejects token limit fields (`max_tokens`, `max_output_tokens`, `max_completion_tokens`) and `metadata`. LiteLLM strips these fields for this provider.
-   `/v1/chat/completions` honors `stream`. When `stream` is false (default), LiteLLM aggregates the Responses stream into a single JSON response.

## Authentication[​](#authentication "Direct link to Authentication")

ChatGPT subscription access uses an OAuth device code flow:

1.  LiteLLM prints a device code and verification URL
2.  Open the URL, sign in, and enter the code
3.  Tokens are stored locally for reuse

## Usage - LiteLLM Python SDK[​](#usage---litellm-python-sdk "Direct link to Usage - LiteLLM Python SDK")

### Responses (recommended for Codex models)[​](#responses-recommended-for-codex-models "Direct link to Responses (recommended for Codex models)")

ChatGPT Responses

```
import litellmresponse = litellm.responses(    model="chatgpt/gpt-5.3-codex",    input="Write a Python hello world")print(response)
```

### Chat Completions (bridged to Responses)[​](#chat-completions-bridged-to-responses "Direct link to Chat Completions (bridged to Responses)")

ChatGPT Chat Completions

```
import litellmresponse = litellm.completion(    model="chatgpt/gpt-5.4",    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Write a Python hello world"}])print(response)
```

## Usage - LiteLLM Proxy[​](#usage---litellm-proxy "Direct link to Usage - LiteLLM Proxy")

model_list:  - model_name: chatgpt/gpt-5.4    model_info:      mode: responses    litellm_params:      model: chatgpt/gpt-5.4  - model_name: chatgpt/gpt-5.4-pro    model_info:      mode: responses    litellm_params:      model: chatgpt/gpt-5.4-pro  - model_name: chatgpt/gpt-5.3-codex    model_info:      mode: responses    litellm_params:      model: chatgpt/gpt-5.3-codex  - model_name: chatgpt/gpt-5.3-codex-spark    model_info:      mode: responses    litellm_params:      model: chatgpt/gpt-5.3-codex-spark  - model_name: chatgpt/gpt-5.3-instant    model_info:      mode: responses    litellm_params:      model: chatgpt/gpt-5.3-instant  - model_name: chatgpt/gpt-5.3-chat-latest    model_info:      mode: responses    litellm_params:      model: chatgpt/gpt-5.3-chat-latest
```

How does the k8s files keeps in sync? we are using the same pattern to deploy like the others -usinf flux?

Good question — this is an important distinction in the plan. There are **two sync patterns** in this repo, and litellm deliberately uses the *manual* one. Let me lay out exactly how each works.

## The two sync mechanisms in this repo

**1. Flux GitOps (used by immich, garage, monitoring, cloudflared)** — pull-based, fully automatic:
```
git push -> GitRepository (flux) -> Kustomization CR -> kustomize-controller
             (anywhere/clusters/s145/<app>.yaml, spec.decryption.provider=sops, secretRef=sops-age)
```
- A `Kustomization` CR in `anywhere/clusters/s145/immich.yaml` points Flux at `./anywhere/k8s/immich`, `prune: true`, `wait: true`. Flux watches the git repo every `3m`, diffs, and applies/removes whatever changed.
- **Why it works for secrets:** those apps' secrets are encrypted with the **`s145_cluster`** age key, and `Secret/flux-system/sops-age` holds that key, so kustomize-controller can **decrypt in-cluster** and apply automatically.

**2. Manual `kubectl apply` (used by vaultwarden, and our litellm plan)** — push-based, human-triggered:
```bash
sops -d .../secret.enc.yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl kustomize anywhere/k8s/litellm | kubectl apply -f -
```

## Why litellm does NOT use Flux (deliberate)

Your instruction was to encrypt litellm's credentials to **`mark` + `pro_darwin` only** — and I kept `s145_cluster` out of that rule. But Flux's SOPS integration **can only decrypt with the `s145_cluster` key** it holds in `flux-system/sops-age`. Consequences:

| | Flux sync | Manual apply |
|---|---|---|
| Encrypts creds to | must include `s145_cluster` | `mark` + `pro_darwin` **only** (your requirement) ✓ |
| Decryption | Flux decrypts at sync | you decrypt with `sops -d` on your Mac |
| App namespaces auto-created | yes | namespace manifest included |
| Update flow | `flux reconcile kustomization litellm` | `kubectl apply` after edit |

So the *durable, non-secret* parts (deployment, service, config) **could** be Flux-managed; only the *secret* forces manual. Two options:

## Option A — Fully manual (current plan, simplest)
Everything under `anywhere/k8s/litellm/` applied with `kubectl apply` when you change it. Matches `vaultwarden`. You're the sync mechanism — must remember to re-apply after edits.

## Option B — Hybrid (ask if you prefer)
- **Flux-manage the non-secret manifests** → `clusters/s145/litellm.yaml` + `kustomization.yaml` (like vaultwarden is now effectively Flux-listed), so deployments auto-sync on push.
- **Manual SOPS step only for the Secret** (decrypt + `kubectl create secret`), since it's `mark`/`pro_darwin`-only.

Option B gives you flux auto-sync of the app and keeps your secret encryption rule intact.

Which do you want — **fully manual** (as planned), or **Flux for manifests + manual secret**? Given your secret rule (`mark`/`pro_darwin`) is the binding constraint, I recommend **Option B** if you value auto-sync of the app, **Option A** if you'd rather not interleave two application methods for one small workload.

Here is the finalized, Flux-integrated plan.

---

# LiteLLM Proxy — Flux-managed, on `oracle-eu-arm1` (FINAL)

## 1. Flux wiring (mirrors `immich` exactly)

**`anywhere/clusters/s145/litellm.yaml`**
```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: Kustomization
metadata: { name: litellm, namespace: flux-system }
spec:
  interval: 3m
  retryInterval: 1m
  timeout: 5m
  dependsOn: [{ name: infra }]
  sourceRef: { kind: GitRepository, name: flux-system }
  decryption:
    provider: sops
    secretRef: { name: sops-age }
  path: ./anywhere/k8s/litellm
  prune: true
  wait: true
```
- Git push → Flux auto-diffs applies whenever you commit. Reconcile on demand:
  `flux reconcile kustomization litellm -n flux-system --with-source`

## 2. SOPS secret — cluster-decryptable

**`.sops.yaml` new creation rule** (note: now includes `s145_cluster`):
```yaml
- path_regex: k8s/litellm/secret.enc.yaml
  encrypted_regex: "^(data|stringData)$"
  key_groups:
    - age: [*pro_darwin, *mark, *s145_cluster]
```
```
sops updatekeys -y anywhere/k8s/litellm/secret.enc.yaml
```
Secret holds `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` (`openssl rand -base64 48`) + `LITELLM_SALT_KEY` (`openssl rand -base64 32`). Flux decrypts it at sync with `sops-age`; you can still decrypt on your Mac with `mark`/`pro_darwin`.

## 3. Manifests (`anywhere/k8s/litellm/`)

**`kustomization.yaml`**
```yaml
resources:
  - namespace.yaml
  - secret.enc.yaml        # SOPS-encrypted; Flux decrypts
  - config.yaml            # → CM via configMapGenerator
  - pvc.yaml
  - deployment.yaml
  - service.yaml
configMapGenerator:
  - name: litellm-config
    namespace: litellm
    files: [ config.yaml ]
    options: { disableNameSuffixHash: true }
```
- **`config.yaml`** — `chatgpt-sol` (`chatgpt/gpt-5.6-sol`, `mode: responses`, token limits, `chatgpt_auth_file_path: /data/chatgpt/auth.json`) + `chatgpt-codex` (`chatgpt/gpt-5.3-codex`, same), `general_settings: { master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY, salt_key: os.environ/LITELLM_SALT_KEY }`.
- **`deployment.yaml`** — `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.94.0` (pinned, no `latest`; arm64 on ghcr); `replicaCount: 1`; `nodeSelector: kubernetes.io/hostname: oracle-eu-arm1`; `envFrom: [litellm-secret]`; env `CHATGPT_TOKEN_DIR=/data/chatgpt`, `CHATGPT_AUTH_FILE=auth.json`; probes `/health/liveliness` + `/health/readiness` (`initialDelaySeconds: 120`); mounts `litellm-token` PVC at `/data/chatgpt`.
- **`service.yaml`** — NodePort `31400` → `4000`, `externalTrafficPolicy: Local`. **No IngressRoute, no public DNS.**
- **`pvc.yaml`** — `local-path`, `1Gi`, on `oracle-eu-arm1` (holds `auth.json` + SQLite).

**Deviations from official docs (accepted, per prior discussion):** SQLite no-Postgres (plain image, master-key auth only), 1 replica (single writable ChatGPT token file → no race on refresh), NodePort/Tailnet instead of LB+managed PG/Redis.

## 4. One-time device login (outside Flux, as a Job)
Flux deploys the stack + PVC; then run a **one-off `litellm-chatgpt-login` Job** (committed manifest, mounts `litellm-token`, `CHATGPT_TOKEN_DIR=/data/chatgpt`) → logs print device code + URL → you complete the flow in a browser → CLI writes `auth.json` into the PVC → delete Job, `kubectl rollout restart deploy/litellm`. Token persists across restart/redeploy; auto-refresh in place.

## 5. Verify (via NodePort over Tailnet)
- `/health/readiness` 200
- unauthorized `/v1/models` → 401
- authorized `/v1/models`, `/v1/responses` (chatgpt-sol), `/v1/chat/completions` (chatgpt-codex) all 200
- `rollout restart` → `auth.json` still present, `/v1/models` still lists aliases (no re-login)

## 6. Rollback / revoke
- Image pinned + immutable: edit `image.tag` in git → Flux rolls; or `kubectl rollout undo`.
- Revoke ChatGPT: delete the `litellm-token` PVC (forces re-login). Cut clients: rotate master key → re-`sops -e` → Flux.

---

One open item to confirm before I start: **PVC size** (I assume `1Gi` is plenty — `auth.json` is a few KB, SQLite is small). Also confirm the NodePort **`31400`** is fine, and that **`gpt-5.3-codex`** stays as your second model (it's NOT deprecated, but note it and `gpt-5.4-*` retire from Codex sign-in Aug 31, 2026 — `gpt-5.6-sol` is unaffected). 1. **`chatgpt_auth_file_path` param name not 100% verified in `v1.94.0`** (it came from PR #24943). # LiteLLM Proxy on `oracle-eu-arm1` — FINAL PLAN (Flux-managed)

## 1. Fallback strategy (ARM fails → hp348)

| Failure at | Detection | Change to make |
|---|---|---|
| arm64 image pull (`ImagePullBackOff`) | `kubectl -n litellm get pods` | Confirm ghcr arm64 manifest; if absent, target **hp348 (amd64)** instead |
| Pod runs but `/health/liveliness` stays red | `kubectl logs` | Fix auth-file-param vs `CHATGPT_TOKEN_DIR` (gap #1) |
| No model output / 4xx on a model | `/v1/models` + responses curl | Prune/enable models; `/v1/responses` is the reliable path |
| ARM node can't schedule PVC (`local-path`) | `get pvc` | repin node |

**Switch node → hp348 = a 4-line edit** (all in the same manifests):
- `deployment.yaml`: `nodeSelector: kubernetes.io/hostname: oracle-eu-arm1` → `kubernetes.io/hostname: hp348`
- `pvc.yaml`: pin references + `storageClassName: local-path` (hp348 is x86_64; ghcr has amd64+arm64, so the same pinned `v1.94.0` image works on both — **no image change**)
- `service.yaml`: `nodePort: 31400` same; client base URL becomes `http://100.91.37.112:31400` (hp349 tätän IP)
- `clusters/s145/litellm.yaml`: no change
- Re-run the PVC-backed login Job (it re-creates on the new node's local-path).

Both nodes are k3s agents on the same cluster; `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` + the pinned pod means only the target host's NodePort serves. h gibt fallback is clean because nothing about the Flux/Kustomization/SOPS/secret changes — only the three manifest files with the node pin.

> Note on data: the token PVC is node-local. Moving nodes means a fresh `local-path` volume + one re-login (expected). The master key stays in SOPS.

## 2. Reusable login Job (same folder, EXCLUDED from Flux)

Committed as `anywhere/k8s/litellm/login-job.yaml` but **NOT listed in `kustomization.yaml`**, so Flux (`prune: true`) will never manage or delete it. It is operator-triggered via `kubectl` only. Adds the same `namespace`, `nodeSelector`, and token PVC mount so it works identically on either node.

**How it works (documented in the file header + `README.md`):**
1. `kubectl -n litellm apply -f anywhere/k8s/litellm/login-job.yaml`
2. `kubectl -n litellm logs -f job/litellm-login` → prints a **device code + verification URL**.
3. Sign in with the ChatGPT Plus account in any browser, enter the code.
4. CLI writes `auth.json` into the `litellm-token` PVC (same one the Deployment mounts at `/data/chatgpt`).
5. Delete the Job: `kubectl -n litellm delete job litellm-login` (token file persists on the PVC).
6. `kubectl -n litellm rollout restart deploy/litellm` → pod picks up the refreshed token.

**Reuse for renewal:** re-run steps 1–6 whenever the ChatGPT session expires or is revoked. Because it's outside the Flux kustomization, it won't be pruned or auto-run; it's an explicit, operator-driven action. Placeholder note in README: "not part of the Flux-managed kustomization — apply manually."

## 3. Deploy sequence

1. `.sops.yaml` **creation rule** for `k8s/litellm/secret.enc.yaml` → `pro_darwin`, `mark`, `s145_cluster`.
2. Generate keys: `openssl rand -base64 48` (master) + `openssl rand -base64 32` (salt); `sops -e` into the Secret.
3. Author all files (target `oracle-eu-arm1`): `kustomization.yaml`, `namespace.yaml`, `config.yaml`, `deployment.yaml`, `service.yaml`, `pvc.yaml`, `secret.enc.yaml`, `login.yaml`, `clusters/s145/litellm.yaml`, `k8s/README.md` notes.
4. `git add` the new files (Flake/fSAT semantics), push, then `flux reconcile kustomization litellm -n flux-system --with-source`.
5. `docker manifest inspect ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.94.0 linux/arm64` gate the ARM pull.
6. Verify readiness → apply login Job → device login → delete Job → rollout restart.
7. Run acceptance checks; if ARM blocked, apply the §1 fallback edit to hp348.

## Final acceptance
- `/health/readiness` 200 · unauthorized `/v1/models` → 401 · authorized `/v1/models` = `{chatgpt-sol, chatgpt-codex}` · `/v1/responses` & `/v1/chat/completions` 200 · `rollout restart` keeps `auth.json` (no re-login).
